pairs.question: Audistisne aliquem, tergo qui sustulit orbem?
pairs.answer: Ille ego sum: Alciden terra recepta uocat.
pairs.derivation: Within Hercules' direct speech to the women of the grove he asks a real interrogative (-ne: 'Have you heard of anyone who lifted the sphere on his back?') and immediately answers it himself by identifying himself ('I am that one; the earth that has received me calls me Alcides'). Self-answered rhetorical question inside the speech. The introductory narration 'uerba minora deo' precedes the speech and is not part of the utterance. Answer ends at the line-final full stop after 'uocat'; what follows ('quis facta Herculeae non audit...') begins a fresh rhetorical sequence, so it is cut.
